newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH LOCAL GOVTS SAY OPPOSED TO NEW BUDGET CUTS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH LOCAL GOVTS SAY OPPOSED TO NEW BUDGET CUTS.

text.p: The Association of Finnish Local Authorities on Wednesday called on the government to stick with its earlier promise to not make any new cuts in state transfers to municipalities.
"In the budget talks in spring it was agreed that the municipal finances will not be the target of new cuts," the association said in a statement.

"The executive board of the association requires that the government stands by its promise," it said, adding the government must not implement new savings by cutting the index adjustments of state transfers to municipalities.
Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said already in February that the government would not make any new cuts in state transfers to municipalities in the 1998 state budget.
But earlier government decisions on cuts in state transfers to local governments affecting 1998 would remain in force, Lipponen said.
The government's pledge to make no new cuts in state grants to municipalities was repeated at the end of budget talks in early June.
But in July, the finance ministry proposed new savings aimed to cut 1998 state budget spending to some 188 billion markka from the earlier agreed 191 billion.
The ministry's proposal included cutting in half, or by 350 million markka, the index adjustments of state transfers to municipalities, the Finnish news agency STT reported.
Finance ministry deputy budget chief Hannu Makinen told Reuters some measures touching municipal finances were planned but he declined to give any details.
The government is scheduled to hold talks on August 13-15 to agree on next year's budget proposal, which will be given to parliament on September 2.
